properties.description: Tungsten nickel oxide or similar W-Ni oxide material

nodes.name: Heteroatom-induced oriented growth of Ni-doped WO3
nodes.procedure: Ni-doped WO3 precursor (denoted as Ni-WO3) supported on carbon cloth (CC) was prepared via a heteroatom-induced oriented-growth strategy, in which ammonium metatungstate (AMT) was selected as a W source and Ni2+ ions were chosen as a structural additive. The obtained materials show distinct diffraction signals of hexagonal WO3 (h-WO3, JCPDS No. 85-2460).
nodes.source_text: As schematically illustrated in Figure 1a, the mirror-symmetric nanoarray networks of atomic Ni-incorporated tungsten oxynitride (Ni-WNO) were constructed by a simple two-step synthesis procedure. In brief, a Ni-doped WO3 precursor (denoted as Ni - WO3 ) supported on carbon cloth (CC) was prepared via a heteroatom-induced oriented-growth strategy, in which ammonium metatungstate (AMT) was selected as a W source and Ni2+ ions were chosen as a structural additive

nodes.name: Nitriding by chemical vapor deposition
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, Ni-WO3 was nitrided by chemical vapor deposition with melamine as an N source to obtain Ni-WNO
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, Ni-WO3 was nitrided by chemical vapor deposition with melamine as an N source to obtain Ni-WNO (Figure S6)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-WO3 shows distinct diffraction signals of hexagonal WO3 (h-WO3, JCPDS No. 85-2460), with Ni dopants increasing the diffraction intensity of the (200) facet relative to the (002) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) was first conducted to gain the structural information of Ni - WO3. The obtained materials show distinct diffraction signals of hexagonal WO3 (h - WO3, JCPDS No. 85-2460), and the introduction of Ni dopants mainly increases the diffraction intensity of the (200) facet relative to the (002) facet (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-WO3 with 5% Ni input features mirror-symmetric nanoarray networks assembled by intergrown hexagonal sheets and nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images in Figure 1f clearly confirm its highly sturdy network structure assembled by the intergrown mirror-symmetric nanoarrays as indicated by the white circle regions in Figure 1f2.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images of Ni-WO3 nanorod along <010> direction show atomic Ni columns at bridging sites, confirming atomically dispersed Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1h shows the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images of a representative Ni - WO3 nanorod acquired along the < 010> direction... certain less intense atomic columns observed at bridging sites in the Ni - WO3 could be identified as Ni atoms.

nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2a, Ni-WNO shows clear diffraction peaks of the cubic WNO (JCPDS No. 25-1254) with compressive strain due to the dopants of Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-WNO shows Raman signals at 680 and 800 cm⁻¹ for symmetric stretching vibration (νs) of O-W-O, with additional binding mode at 883 cm⁻¹ attributed to W-O-Ni stretching due to Ni dopants.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2b, Raman signals at 680 and 800 cm⁻¹ in both WNO and Ni-WNO are associated with the symmetric stretching vibration (νs) of O-W-O. Conspicuously, Ni-WNO displays an additional binding mode centered at 883 cm⁻¹, which could be attributed to the lattice mismatch of W-O-Ni stretching induced by Ni dopants.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-WNO W 4f XPS shows W⁶⁺ peaks at 37.7 and 35.5 eV, and W⁴⁺ peaks at 34.2 and 32.2 eV indicating tungsten oxynitride formation; Ni 2p shows Niⁿ⁺ (n>0) peaks at 870.4/853.3 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the deconvoluted W 4f XPS peaks (Table S2), the pair peaks in Ni-WNO at 37.7 and 35.5 eV are ascribed to the W 4f5/2 and W 4f7/2 of W6+, respectively, while the pair peaks at lower binding energy (34.2 and 32.2 eV) can be assigned to the W 4f5/2 and W 4f7/2 of W4+... Ni-WNO displays a positively charged Ni state relative to the Ni CS, which implies that the pair peaks at 870.4 and 853.3 eV are associated with Ni 2p1/2 and Ni 2p3/2 of Nin+ (n > 0).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES indicates average Ni valence state in Ni-WNO between Ni⁰ (Ni foil ≈ Ni CS) and Ni²⁺ (Ni(OH)₂); W L₃-edge XANES shows higher W oxidation state in Ni-WNO than WNO but lower than WO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In XANES profiles (Figure 2c), the Ni K-edge position follows the order of Ni foil ≈ Ni CS < Ni-WNO < Ni(OH)2, which indicates that the average valence state of nickel (Ni n+) in Ni-WNO lies between 0 and +2. Conspicuously, Ni-WNO exhibits a much lower white line intensity relative to the WO3 counterpart, but marginally higher than WNO, demonstrating that the incorporation of Ni results in a higher oxidation state of W in Ni-WNO.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-N/O scattering at 1.65 Å in Ni-WNO with no Ni-Ni path confirming atomic Ni dispersion; Ni-WNO shows shorter W-W/Ni scattering paths at 2.30 and 2.86 Å vs WNO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In FT-EXAFS profiles (Figure 2d), a broad peak appears at 1.65 Å (not phase-corrected) with a prominent shoulder on the low-R side, which is associated with Ni-N and Ni-O single scattering. Meanwhile, the absence of Ni-Ni path verifies the atomically dispersed Ni sites in the Ni-WNO... Ni-WNO exhibits a shorter W-W/Ni scattering path at about 2.30 and 2.86 Å (phase-corrected: 2.67 and 3.16 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-WNO composed of nanocrystals with average size of 4 nm; SAED pattern matches cubic WNO phase with no crystalline Ni particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 2h,i), it can be observed that Ni-WNO is composed of Ni-incorporated WNO nanocrystals with an average size of about 4 nm... The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of Ni-WNO... match well with the cubic WNO phase without any signal of crystalline Ni particles or clusters.
